tagline: From Cedar Creek past Signal Knob to the Shenandoah’s forks
intro: On the approach to Star Tannery, SR 55 descends Great North Mountain through George Washington National Forest as a two-lane road. From Cedar Creek, the drive continues past Little North Mountain, through Strasburg and across the North Fork Shenandoah River in an S-curve. Most of SR 55 is a Virginia Byway. The road shares its western approach to Strasburg with US 48, whose eastern end is at I-81. Inside Strasburg it briefly shares Massanutten Street with US 11.

Rail transport helped connect the towns along this corridor: service reached Riverton from Manassas in 1854 and soon extended to Strasburg. Strasburg’s pottery factory later became a railway depot, then a museum in 1970. The present highway crosses beneath the railway’s B-Line more than once as it passes through Strasburg.

Drive from Star Tannery past Wheatfield, where the road turns south, then through Lebanon Church toward Strasburg. In town, SR 55 turns east on King Street before reaching the North Fork crossing. Beyond Signal Knob, it crosses Passage Creek and enters Riverton, where the North and South Forks join. SR 55 then turns south, crosses the South Fork and continues into downtown Front Royal.

moments.title: Strasburg
moments.text: Strasburg’s nickname, Pot Town, came from making both everyday and decorative earthenware and stoneware. One factory building traces what happened next: built in 1891 for the Strasburg Stone and Earthenware Manufacturing Company, it changed to railroad use in 1913. The two-story brick structure served as a Southern Railroad station and depot before the Strasburg Museum opened there in 1970. Its displays include local pottery alongside railroad artifacts and a model railroad, bringing those successive uses together in one building. The factory’s slate-covered hipped roof has a raised monitor along its top.

moments.title: Signal Knob
moments.text: Signal Knob’s view into the northern Shenandoah Valley made it a military observation point during the Civil War. Both Union and Confederate armies used the peak; Confederate signalmen occupied it from 1862 to 1864 and communicated with other stations using flags, lanterns and telescopes. In October 1864, John Brown Gordon studied Union positions at Cedar Creek from here before devising a surprise attack. The attack succeeded that morning, but a Union counterattack defeated the Confederates later the same day. The Massanutten Trail leads to the peak, where Civil War fortification remains survive.

moments.title: Front Royal
moments.text: At Riverton, the North and South Forks meet to form the Shenandoah River. Rail service reached this part of Front Royal in 1854, and the line soon extended to Strasburg. The Riverton Historic District includes houses dating from the mid-19th century, along with the Carson Lime Company’s worker housing and an old post office and grocery. From Riverton, SR 55 crosses the South Fork on its way into downtown, moving from the river junction into the town’s street grid. The district’s Riverton United Methodist Church dates from 1883–1890.
